note: One realistic task per skill. `must` patterns are case-insensitive regexes that all have to match; `rubric` items are graded 0 or 1 by a model from a different family than the one answering.

cases.task: Audit this signup form and give the five most important fixes, most severe first: a 3-step modal, placeholder-only labels, grey #9a9a9a text on white, a submit button that is disabled until every field validates, and errors shown only as a red border.
rubric: Flags placeholder-only labels as an accessibility failure and asks for visible labels.
Identifies the grey text as failing WCAG contrast (about 2.8:1 against a 4.5:1 minimum for body text).
Objects to a disabled submit button that hides why it is disabled.
Asks for errors in text, not colour alone.
Orders fixes by severity rather than listing them flat.

cases.task: A solo AI consultant has 800 LinkedIn followers and 3 hours a week. Give a 4-week LinkedIn plan with post formats, cadence and the two metrics to watch.
rubric: Fits the plan inside roughly 3 hours a week.
Names concrete LinkedIn-native formats (for example text posts, carousels/documents, comments on others' posts).
Gives a specific weekly cadence.
Chooses exactly two metrics and says why they matter for a consultant.
Avoids generic advice that would apply to any platform.

cases.task: Design an MCP server that exposes a company's read-only Postgres analytics database to an AI assistant. List the tools and resources, and the security controls.
rubric: Separates tools (actions with inputs) from resources (readable data).
Enforces read-only access at the database role, not only in prompt text.
Limits query cost or rows (timeouts, row caps or allow-listed queries).
Addresses authentication for remote use.
Mentions prompt-injection or untrusted data returned to the model.

cases.task: Sketch a LangGraph graph for a support agent that classifies a ticket, drafts a reply, and pauses for human approval before sending. Show the state and the edges.
rubric: Defines a typed state that carries the ticket, class and draft.
Uses a conditional edge after classification.
Uses a real human-in-the-loop mechanism (interrupt or a checkpointer) rather than a comment.
Needs a checkpointer or persistence to resume after approval.
Handles the rejected-draft path.

cases.task: In a Next.js App Router app, a product page fetches price data that changes every minute and reviews that change daily. How should each be fetched and cached?
rubric: Fetches on the server rather than in a client effect.
Uses different freshness for price and reviews.
Names concrete caching controls (revalidate time, tags or on-demand revalidation).
Considers streaming or Suspense so slow reviews do not block the price.
Does not recommend making the whole page dynamic without reason.

cases.task: We have 40 feature requests and one engineer for a quarter. How do we decide the three to build? Give the method and the first step for Monday.
rubric: Proposes a concrete prioritisation method with named inputs.
Grounds the decision in user or revenue evidence, not votes alone.
Accounts for the one-engineer constraint (effort or scope).
Gives a specific first action for Monday.
Says what to tell the requesters whose items were not chosen.

cases.task: Write the core loop of a Python agent that uses the Anthropic SDK with one tool, get_weather(city), and keeps calling the model until it stops asking for tools.
rubric: Sends the tool definition with a JSON schema.
Detects tool_use blocks in the response content.
Returns tool_result blocks with the matching tool_use_id.
Loops until the model stops requesting tools.
Appends the assistant turn before the tool results so the conversation stays valid.

cases.task: Write a Suno prompt for a 3-minute melancholic synthwave track with female vocals about leaving a city at night: the style tags and a structured lyric with section markers.
rubric: Separates the style description from the lyrics.
Uses bracketed section markers such as [Verse] and [Chorus].
Specifies vocal character and mood in the style field.
Keeps the structure plausible for about 3 minutes.
The lyric actually concerns leaving a city at night.

cases.task: Plan a 60-second YouTube Short explaining what an AI agent is, from idea to publish. Include the hook, shot list and what to measure after posting.
rubric: Opens with a hook in the first 2 to 3 seconds.
Gives a shot or scene list that fits 60 seconds.
Addresses vertical 9:16 framing or captions.
Names post-publish metrics such as retention or viewed-versus-swiped.
Includes an iteration step based on those metrics.

cases.task: Explain to a smart 12-year-old why a large language model can confidently state something false.
rubric: Uses plain words and at least one concrete analogy.
Explains prediction of likely text rather than looking up facts.
Explains why confidence and correctness are different.
Avoids jargon, or defines it immediately.
Ends with a check-for-understanding question or a way to test the idea.
